lyrics:
[Intro: solo clean electric guitar, delicate chord melody]

[Verse 1: plain, close, guitar only]
The number nine pulls out at half past one
I know every stop, I know every sun-
burned seat and every flickering sign
This town and I keep the same hours, most nights

[Verse 2: bass and soft hi-hat enter]
She's seen the things I've done and where
She's seen me worse and didn't stare
The river keeps what the river's told
The streetlights hum and the night is old

[Chorus: full band, warm, voice lifts]
Ride on, ride on
Past the stop where I came undone
Keep the doors closed, keep it slow
There's a corner I don't need to know
Ride on

[Verse 3: full band, steady]
There's a woman with her shoes inside her bag
A kid asleep against a paper flag
Nobody talks and everybody stays
We're all going home in different ways

[Chorus: full band, warm, voice lifts]
Ride on, ride on
Past the stop where I came undone
Keep the doors closed, keep it slow
There's a corner I don't need to know
Ride on

[Guitar Solo: melodic, clean with a little grit]

[Bridge: drums drop to rim clicks, voice lower]
That's the place, the place I left it
Under the sign, the winter I lost
I don't go looking, I don't forget it
I just don't pay what it cost

[Outro: choir enters, lead ad-libs over it, building]
(Carry me, carry me home)
Not alone, not alone
(Carry me, carry me home)
I'm not going back there
(Carry me, carry me home)
Not alone, not alone
(Carry me, carry me home)
Ride on
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 84 BPM, 4/4, E major. Gentle, unhurried, a late-night walking pace that widens into a hymn.

VOICE: Male tenor with a plain, unpolished, conversational tone and a slight catch. No showing off. Low and private in the bridge. In the outro he sings short lines between the phrases of a mixed choir with a gospel feel.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar playing a chord-melody in the style of late-60s soul-rock, with little slides and hammer-ons. Warm, melodic bass that plays counter-lines. Drums that start as a hi-hat and grow to a full, relaxed groove. A second guitar with light overdrive for the solo. A mixed choir. Soft organ under the outro.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, solo guitar. 0:20 Verse 1, voice and guitar. 0:46 Verse 2, bass and hi-hat. 1:12 Chorus 1, full band. 1:36 Verse 3. 2:02 Chorus 2. 2:26 Guitar solo. 2:48 Bridge, drums down to rim clicks, the hard memory. 3:14 Outro, the choir enters and repeats one line while the lead answers and the band builds. The band drops away and the choir ends alone at 4:15.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-90s rock recorded in a big room: natural, warm and open, guitar very present, choir wide and reverberant.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The choir's entrance at 3:14.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The narrator is years past the worst of it. He is not confessing, he is riding by. Verse 3 looks at the other passengers, which the original, written from inside the loneliness, could not.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Solitude, companionship, a hard memory passed, then being carried.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

A man rides the last bus through a city that knows him well, past a stop he does not get off at any more.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: recovery, with the stop as the place it went wrong; grief; a night-shift worker's commute; someone new in a city with nobody to call. The choir at the end can be the other passengers or something larger.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: a place as the companion, a gentle surface over a hard memory, a solo guitar opening and a choir ending. Designed mishearing: 'ride on' is heard as 'right on' and 'write home', and the outro's 'not alone' as 'not at home'.
